d: The MicroProfiler includes several different modes, all of which offer different ways to understand your game's performance profile.
h:
The MicroProfiler includes several modes, which can help you visualize your game's performance characteristics in different ways. After opening the MicroProfiler, use the Modes menu to switch between them.

Frame mode and detailed mode are covered under MicroProfiler basics.

Timers mode

Timers mode is an alternative way of visualizing the data in the detailed view: as a list of labels with processing times and call counts. Horizontal bar graphs in some columns help you spot the busiest tasks.

Controls are similar to detailed view:

  • Left-click and hold to pan up and down.
  • Left-click a label to add it to the line graph in the lower-right.
  • Use the Groups menu to filter the list.
  • Use the Timers menu to customize the columns.

All of the information in this view is visible when you hover over a label in the detailed view.

Counters mode

Counters mode is a lengthy list of categories and statistics, including instance count and memory usage (in bytes) for the various tasks.

  • Just like the detailed view, left-click and hold to pan up and down.
  • Left-click in the Graph column to add a small usage graph with minimum and maximum values. Left-click the graph again to expand it.
  • Right-click a graph to close it.
  • You can't filter this view, but you can left-click on a category (for example, memory) to collapse it.

While counters mode can be useful, the Developer Console is the best way to identify memory issues. You might also find the X-ray view helpful for identifying when problematic memory allocation occurs.

Groups mode

Only available in the web UI. Similar to timers mode, groups mode provides average, max, and total task times for each group, broken down by thread, to help you identify how broad categories of tasks are impacting your frame times.

Threads mode

Only available in the web UI. Similar to timers mode, threads mode provides average and total task times for each thread, broken down by group, to help you identify how your game is distributing tasks across threads.

Hidden mode

Only available in the desktop UI. Hidden mode keeps the MicroProfiler menu open, but hides the bar graph. It's useful for reducing visual clutter, saving frame data, and pausing and unpausing while you observe the line graph.

kid.simple: The MicroProfiler can show the same timing data in several different ways, called modes. You switch between them with the Modes menu. Some modes show lists of tasks and how long they took, some show counters like memory, and some are only in the web version. Picking the right mode makes it easier to spot what is slowing your game down.
kid.analogy: It is like looking at your grades as a bar chart, a list, or a report card. It is the same information, just arranged differently so different things stand out.
keyPoints: Open the MicroProfiler, then use the Modes menu to switch views.
Frame mode and detailed mode are explained on the main MicroProfiler page.
Timers mode lists task labels with their times and how many times they were called. Click a label to add it to the line graph.
Counters mode lists stats like instance counts and memory in bytes. Click the Graph column to add a small graph.
For memory problems, the Developer Console is still the best tool.
Groups mode and threads mode are only in the web UI. They show average, max, and total times by group or by thread.
Hidden mode is only in the desktop UI. It hides the bar graph to reduce clutter while keeping the menu open.

terms.mode: A different way of displaying the same profiler data.
terms.label: A name for a task in the profiler, like `Heartbeat` or a script name.
terms.call count: How many times a task ran. A label called 300 times in a frame is a clue it might be doing too much.
terms.counter: A number the profiler keeps track of, like how many instances exist or how many bytes of memory are used.
terms.byte: A tiny unit of memory. 1,048,576 bytes is 1 MiB.
terms.thread: One line of work the computer can do at the same time as others. Roblox splits work across several threads.
terms.web UI: The version of the MicroProfiler you open in a web browser from a saved dump file.
terms.desktop UI: The version of the MicroProfiler shown on top of the game itself.

watchOut: Looking for groups or threads mode in the in-game overlay. They only exist in the web UI from a saved dump.
Using counters mode as your main memory tool. Use the Developer Console Memory tab for memory issues.
Forgetting that timers mode shows the same info you get by hovering labels in detailed mode.
